chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan from Abu Burdah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about renting out a defined piece of land for known dirhams, and he said, 'There is no harm in it.' I asked him about renting it out for food, and he said, 'If it is from its own food, there is no good in it.'

key_terms.مِنْ طَعَامِهَا: from its own food (produce of the same land)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on renting land for food instead of money in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between fixed-rent land leasing (*ijarah*) and share-cropping (*muzara'ah*), permitting the former while cautioning against the latter when the payment is derived directly from the leased land's produce. This prohibition aims to prevent *gharar* (uncertainty) and ensure the tenant bears the risk of cultivation, a key principle in Shia fiqh. The ruling reflects the broader juristic consensus on maintaining clear ownership and risk allocation in agricultural contracts.
